title: Emergent Misalignment Under LoRA Fine-Tuning: Does Parameter Efficiency Change the Effect?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: LoRA is how virtually all practitioners fine-tune large models. Whether LoRA induces emergent misalignment directly determines practical risk for the broad community. If low-rank is safer, that is an important finding. Maximally relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses existing codebase with minor modifications to add LoRA configuration. PEFT/LoRA is well-documented and standard in TRL. Three LoRA rank configurations are simple parameter changes. Highly accessible for beginners with the open codebase.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three training runs differing only in LoRA rank, same evaluation. Single variable ablation. Clear deliverable: misalignment rate vs. LoRA rank. Well within 30 hours. LoRA training is faster than full fine-tuning.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
